property_summary: For any caller and positive nonzero recipient, a successful sendTo call on the reference always either forwards funds using EVM transfer semantics (which revert on failure) so that the call to sendTo either succeeds and decreases contract balance or reverts; replacing transfer with low-level call can mask a failing send (returning false) causing the reference to revert while the mutant may optionally behave differently — specifically, when the callee's fallback reverts, the reference's transfer will revert, but the mutant's call returns false and the mutant can be observed to leave the call as a failure observable via the returned success flag — we assert that calling sendTo to a reverting recipient always reverts (i.e., does not succeed), which holds for the reference but is broken by the mutant's different low-level-call semantics.

For any nonzero amount and nonzero receiver address, if the receiver's fallback ALWAYS reverts, then calling sendTo(receiver, amount) on the reference contract always reverts (transfer bubbles failure), while the mutant using low-level call may return false instead of reverting, so the mutant can allow the outer transaction to succeed or behave differently.

For any nonzero amount sent by the owner to any recipient whose fallback always reverts, calling sendTo(...) on the correct contract always reverts (i.e., the external call does not succeed), whereas the mutant using low-level call can return success=false and thus allow the outer transaction to succeed or behave differently; we assert that sendTo to a reverting receiver never succeeds.

For any caller who is the owner and any positive amount, calling sendTo on a recipient whose fallback uses more than the 2300 gas stipend (causing transfer to revert) must always revert on the reference (transfer bubbles/reverts) but the mutant using low-level call may return false and allow the outer call to succeed; thus the property: when recipient's fallback consumes >2300 gas, sendTo must revert for all amounts and owner calls — the mutant can violate this by not reverting.

For any caller who is the owner and any positive amount, calling sendTo on a recipient whose fallback reverts must always revert (the reference bubbles failure via transfer), but the mutant using low-level call can observe the callee revert without bubbling and thus may let sendTo succeed — so the reference never returns/finishes successfully to a reverting recipient, whereas the mutant can.
